---
title: "Architecture"
description: "Where everything sits — the Mac, the phone, the Spark and the Synology — and the paths a request takes. Built parts are solid; planned parts are dashed, with their phase."
---

The overview first, then one picture of where everything sits, then the three paths a request can
take. Every scenario follows one of those paths, so the table at the end names the path for each,
and each scenario's page says what happens along it. **Solid** parts are built and running;
**dashed** parts are planned, labelled with the phase that brings them. A built part that a later
phase changes stays solid, and its label adds the change with that phase. [The plan](design/plan.md)
holds the reasons.

## The overview

The tools, and how a request reaches a model. The home page shows the same diagram, from one
file, `website/_overview.qmd`.

{{< include _overview.qmd >}}

- **Everything on the Spark listens on 127.0.0.1**, except SSH and `tailscale serve`'s port 443.
  The tailnet's rules let my own devices reach the Spark on those two ports only, and ufw allows
  SSH alone from the LAN.
- **Three accounts on the Spark.** Mine, the admin; `spark`, which runs llama-swap, the engines and
  the brake; and `agent`, for coding agents in tmux, with no sudo, no docker and keys of its own.
  Root runs the web services from its own copies of their units. From Phase 2a, `spark` also runs
  the gate, beside the brake, and two system users of their own run the front (`spark-front`) and
  the model downloads (`spark-pull`). *(They do since Phase 2a's cutover, 2026-10-16, and the
  failure notifier runs as a user systemd makes for each of its runs, `DynamicUser=`.)*
- **From Phase 2a ~~(planned)~~, the front takes 127.0.0.1:9100** with the same keys, so pi, the
  web UI and `agent` change nothing. systemd holds 9100 and the gate's two sockets, so they are
  never free, even while the front or the gate restarts, or crashes again and again. llama-swap moves to 127.0.0.1:900 and the engines to
  800 and up, below 1024, where no other user can listen, and only the internal keys reach
  llama-swap. The gate decides every load, unloads idle models and lifts the brake's hold; the
  brake stays a unit of its own, so it runs even while the gate is down, and then sends its own
  alert. The web containers can't take those ports either: they have dropped their capabilities
  since 2026-10-15, built ahead of the cutover from `main` (Task 37). ntfy
  on the Synology
  carries notifications to my phone, over the tailnet or the home LAN only, and to my Mac ~~from
  Phase 2b~~. [The plan](design/plan.md#the-front-and-the-gate-phase-2a) says why. *(2026-10-14,
  Dan's decision: ntfy optional, moving with the NAS phase; Phases 4 and 5 swapped, the NAS phase
  now 5. ntfy, the phone's and the Mac's alerts and the watchdog all come with Phase 5, NAS and
  backups, so the diagram labels them Phase 5, as it does the shares and backups; until then the
  stack runs without ntfy, the gate, the brake and the failure notifier send nothing and say so,
  and what they would report shows in `spark status` and `make doctor`. The bake-off's vLLM and
  SGLang are Phase 4's.)* *(Built 2026-10-16, at Phase 2a's cutover, its Task 38: all of this runs
  on `brightroar` but ntfy and its alerts, which stay dashed, Phase 5's. Checked as `agent` that
  day: binding 9100 while the front restarted, and 900 while llama-swap restarted, both failed. Not
  yet checked on the box: the front crashing again and again, which Task 49's crash-loop check
  runs, and the gate's sockets through its restart; nor has the brake been seen acting, Tasks 47
  and 48.)*
- **Phase 4a (planned, 2026-10-14)** brings the fast coder, Qwen3.8-27B on SGLang in a container
  that root's unit runs, and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on llama.cpp, which loads after `spark make-room`
  clears the box; opencode on the Mac lists them. Until then both run by hand, outside the stack:
  [The fast coder, by hand](how-to/qwen3.8-27b-sglang.md) and
  [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, by hand](how-to/qwen3.8-flash-next.md).
- **Claude never uses the Spark's models.** Claude Code and Claude Desktop talk straight to
  Anthropic, wherever they run; Orca only starts them. The Spark is a separate mode.

## Reaching the Spark

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 5

  piT["pi, opencode or Hermes on the Mac<br/>in a terminal or Orca"]
  ui["web UI<br/>on the Mac or the phone"]
  piA["pi as agent<br/>in tmux on the Spark"]
  cc["Claude Code<br/>anywhere"]
  app["an app with its own key<br/>Phase 3"]:::planned
  fam["family and friends<br/>over a shared Tailscale node · Phase 6"]:::planned
  guest["a guest at an event<br/>venue LAN, a key each · Phase 6"]:::planned

  tunnel["SSH tunnel<br/>over Tailscale, or the LAN alias"]
  guestui["guest web UI<br/>events only · Phase 6"]:::planned
  serve["tailscale serve, 443<br/>Tailscale only"]
  owui["Open WebUI"]
  searx["SearXNG"]
  front["the front, 127.0.0.1:9100<br/>the same keys, then an internal key"]
  swap["llama-swap, 127.0.0.1:900<br/>internal keys only"]
  litellm["LiteLLM on a LAN port · Phase 3<br/>ahead of the front, in its place, or not at all"]:::planned
  anthropic(("Anthropic"))

  piT --> tunnel --> front
  ui --> serve --> owui --> front
  owui --> searx
  piA --> front
  cc --> anthropic
  front --> swap
  app -.-> litellm
  litellm -. "through the front or in its place, if Phase 3 adds it" .-> swap
  fam -.-> serve
  fam -.-> litellm
  guest -.-> guestui -.-> litellm
  guest -.-> litellm
```

pi on the Mac reaches ~~llama-swap~~ the models only while `make tunnel` runs, since nothing on the
Spark listens beyond 127.0.0.1 but SSH. The web UI needs Tailscale: on another tailnet, over WireGuard, the LAN
alias still carries SSH and so pi's tunnel, but the web UI waits. `agent`'s pi needs no tunnel. opencode and
Hermes on the Mac go through the same tunnel, with ~~the same key~~ a key each *(corrected 2026-10-23: since
2026-10-14 `make clients` set them all to one key, and since the keys' runbook each harness has its own: pi
`SPARK_API_KEY`, OpenCode `SPARK_OPENCODE_KEY`, Hermes `SPARK_HERMES_KEY`)*. From
Phase 2a ~~(planned)~~, the same tunnel, address and keys reach the front instead, which checks the key
and forwards to llama-swap on its new port with a key of its own; no client changes. Only the
inference routes go through: llama-swap's admin routes stay out of every client's reach. *(Built
2026-10-16, at Phase 2a's cutover: pi on the Mac answered through the tunnel that day, the web UI
chatted, searched and transcribed from the phone, and `/unload` through 9100 got
`route_not_served`.)* From Phase
3, apps reach the models with a key of their own; Phase 3 decides whether LiteLLM sits ahead of the
front, takes its place, or isn't used at all, the front growing what Phase 3 needs. From Phase 6,
family and friends reach the web UI and LiteLLM over a shared Tailscale node that shows them only
the Spark, and guests at an event reach LiteLLM and a guest web UI of their own, on the venue's
network only.

## Loading a model

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 5

  req["a request names a model"] --> front["the front, on 9100, checks the key and the route<br/>and counts the requests in flight"]
  front -- loaded --> answer["the engine answers"]
  front -- "not loaded" --> ask{"the gate: brake clear, and the footprint fits what's free for a load:<br/>available memory less the reserve, the growth the loaded models are owed,<br/>any load starting and any make-room hold that isn't mine?<br/>one load at a time, my keys first"}
  front -- "gate down" --> gdown["gate down: loaded models keep serving,<br/>new loads refused with gate_down, a 503;<br/>at boot, nothing loads"]
  ask -- yes --> gload["the gate gives spark launch a ticket and loads it through llama-swap;<br/>spark launch keeps the hold check and a zero-wait fit check"]
  gload --> answer
  gload -- "load fails" --> inline["refused inline, like any API error: a 409, which clients don't retry,<br/>memory needed against what's free for a load, the top holders, one next step and a code"]
  ask -- no --> hold["the gate keeps the request waiting<br/>for its key's wait: 30 s for mine, 10 minutes for agent's"]
  hold -- "fits in time" --> gload
  hold -- "time is up" --> inline
  low["free memory falls<br/>toward the freeze band"] --> brake["the brake warns, then holds new loads<br/>and unloads models, idle ones first,<br/>and acts on the rate of fall"]
  brake -- "holds new loads" --> ask
  brake --> release["the gate lifts the hold after 5 minutes above 28 GiB, if the reloads fit,<br/>once an hour at most; a hold found at boot waits for me"]
  ask --- idle["the gate also unloads on-demand models idle for 60 minutes<br/>and runs make-room, which holds the room for me;<br/>both drain the model first, so neither cuts off a request in flight"]
```

A model loads only if it fits: nothing is evicted to make room, and nothing is swapped for a
smaller model. Free memory is the smaller of `MemAvailable` and what the GPU can allocate, and the
reserve stays free, because overcommitting a GB10 can freeze it without an out-of-memory kill.

*(2026-10-16, at Phase 2a's cutover, its Task 38: the front's and the gate's path, dashed until
then, is built and running, and the diagram shows it alone. Phase 1's path, a request reaching
llama-swap, which started the model through `spark launch`'s brake check and static fit and refused
with a plain error, its reason in `make status`, ended that day. Those two checks stay in `spark
launch`, as backstops behind the gate's ticket. git history keeps the diagram as it was.)*

From Phase 2a ~~(planned, dashed)~~, a request reaches the front first. A model that's loaded is
forwarded at once; for one that isn't, the front asks the gate, which admits one load at a time,
my keys ahead of `agent`'s. What's *free for a load* is then available memory less the reserve,
the growth the loaded models are still owed, and any room make-room is holding for me, which my
own requests may load into and `agent`'s may not. If the model doesn't fit, the request waits
for its key's wait, then gets a refusal that says why, in the client itself. `spark launch` starts
nothing without the gate's ticket, and keeps ~~today's~~ Phase 1's checks *(reworded 2026-10-16, at
the cutover, when they stopped being today's path)* as backstops that never wait. The
reserve stays 24 GiB: the design lowered it to 22, and it went back to 24 the same day.

## Apps and speech (Phase 3, planned)

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 5

  app["an app or pipeline<br/>with its own key"]:::planned --> litellm["LiteLLM: limits and a wait per key,<br/>refusals inline, the real model named"]:::planned
  litellm -.-> pg[("Postgres<br/>keys and usage")]:::planned
  litellm -. "through the front or in its place, if Phase 3 adds it" .-> swap["llama-swap"]
  swap --> chat["chat and embeddings"]
  swap --> stt["whisper, interactive"]
  swap -.-> batch["whisper, batch"]:::planned
  swap -.-> diar["speaker labels"]:::planned
```

Today the web UI and pi reach llama-swap directly with llama-swap's own keys. From Phase 2a they
reach the front instead, with the same keys, and it already waits per key and refuses inline.
*(Since 2026-10-16, Phase 2a's cutover, they do, and llama-swap takes only the internal keys.)* From
Phase 3, my own pipelines and homelab apps come in through LiteLLM, each with a key of its own; it
never logs what they send. Phase 3 decides whether LiteLLM sits ahead of the front, takes its
place, or isn't used at all, the front growing what Phase 3 needs.
